de: de — of, from · also de — by (the agent with a passive participle; = por) · also de — 'by (night)' (de noch), partitive 'of, among' (quinze moros … de los que alcançava; pocas de gentes), 'as' (de ganançia 'as booty'), 'from outside' (de fuera), 'on the right' (de diestro) · also 'about, concerning' (de mí non digan mal 'let them not speak ill of me') · also de — 'as if in' (commo de arrancada 'as if in rout'); 'in the manner of' (de guisa 'in such a way'); 'of, among' (de bivos pocos 'of the living few'); nominalized infinitive (del prender 'of the taking') · also de — 'with' of manner (de fuertes coraçones 'with stout hearts'); 'on' (de pie 'on foot'); 'from' of side (della e della part 'from both sides'); de cabo 'anew' (de + cabo, 'again'); de suso de 'above'; seños … de seños colpes 'with one blow each' · also de — 'in respect of' after an adjective (sobejana de mala 'exceedingly bad'); 'with regard to, about' (me plaze de mio Çid 'I am pleased about the Cid'); 'from, at the hand of' (de señor non ha graçia 'he gets no favor from a lord'); 'from' of origin (de moros fo 'it came from Moors'); 'at' of manner (de vagar 'at leisure', de + the noun vagar) · also de’ — Pidal's de’llaño, read as del llaño 'of the plain' (the article's l run into the ll; a reading, not certain) · de + infinitive after an adjective (de ir somos guisados 'we are ready to go') · also de + infinitive after a verb: començar de 'to begin to' (compeçó de fablar 'he began to speak'), piénssanse de 'set about' (piénssanse de armar), aver de 'to have to' (lo que ha de far 'what he has to do') · also de — 'within' of a time limit (De aquestos quinze días, most likely 'within these fifteen days'; sense uncertain); de veluntad 'willingly'; de + superlative partitive (de los mejores guarnimientos 'of the best equipment')
la: el/la — the (fem.); her/it (object pronoun) · also la que 'the one that' (Çelfa la que dizen de Canal 'Çelfa, the one they call of the Canal')
boca: boca — mouth (besóle la boca 'he kissed his mouth'; = boca)
álbar: Álbar — Álvar (personal name, Álbar Fáñez; = Álvar)
minaya: Minaya — the title by which the Cid's kinsman Álvar Fáñez is called, usually explained as mi + anaya 'my brother'
ya: ya — O! (vocative particle, Arabic yā); also 'now, already' · also ya — 'would', reduced imperfect of aver as conditional ending, 3rd sg., after infinitive + clitic (pagar se ya 'would be satisfied'; = -ía)
avengalvón: Avengalvón — the Moorish lord (alcaide) of Molina, friend and ally of the Cid (proper name, Aven- = Arabic ibn 'son of'; = Abengalbón)
sodes: seer — you are (2nd pl. present, used respectfully to one person; = sois; old -edes ending, cf. odredes, vedes, catedes)
sin: sin — without · also sin — 'besides, apart from' (sin las peonadas 'besides the foot-soldiers'); sin falla 'without fail'; sin dubda
falla: falla — failure, lack (noun; sin falla 'without fail'; = falla, closest falta)
si: si — if; si + subjunctive alone = 'if only …!' · si non — otherwise, if not (si non, do sopiéredes 'if not, wherever you learn'); si + future subjunctive 'if' (si nos falláredes 'if you find us') · also si — si'nulla = sin + nulla with -n assimilated before n- (si'nulla dubda 'without any fear' (or 'doubt'); = sin ningún miedo, sin ninguna duda)
dios: Dios — God · also Dios! — interjection of wonder (Dios, cómmo se alabavan! 'God, how they boasted!')
me: me — me, to me · also reflexive 'myself' (fata que yo me pague 'until I am satisfied')
al: a + el — to the; al menos 'even the least' · also a + el standing for a + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (al espada = a la espada) · also al — 'other thing, the rest' (neuter, Latin alius; de lo al non pienssan nada 'of anything else they think nothing'; distinct from a + el) · also a + el before an infinitive 'on, upon' (al exir de Salón 'on leaving the Jalón'; = al salir) · al 'the other thing, the rest' in al feredes adelant 'the rest you will do later'
çid: Çid — the Cid, 'lord' (Arabic sīdī 'my lord'; pronounced Tsid)
e: e — and (= modern y) · also aver — I have (1st sg. present, apocopated form of he, perfect auxiliary: Espeso e el oro, 'I have spent the gold') · also aver — 'I will', the future auxiliary in a split future (quitarvos e … darvos e de mano 'I will free you … I will let you go'; = vos quitaré, vos daré) · also the full verb 'I have' (el sabor que dend e 'the delight I have of it')
lo: lo — him, it (object pronoun) · lo que perdedes 'that which you lose' (neuter antecedent of the relative) · also lo — neuter article 'what is' (lo to 'what is yours'); pleonastic 'it' (lo an, lo han a far; por tal lo faze 'for that reason he does it')
vea: veer — may I/he see (present subjunctive 1st/3rd sg.; = vea)
el: el — the (masc.) · also el — 'he who' before a relative (el qui quisiere, el que es sobre Fenares); el before a fem. noun beginning with a vowel (el espada = la espada; el algara = la algara) · also el de + place name 'he of, the one from' (mio Çid el de Bivar)
que: que — that, who, which; for · also por que — because, since (= porque) · por que — by which, whereby (por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more') · also que — 'so that, lest' introducing purpose/result (que por miedo non dexen nada; por tal lo faze … que no lo ventasse nadi); after después/mientra 'after, while' (después que, mientra que) · also que — than, after a comparative (mas le vienen … que nos le van 'more come to him than leave him') · also que — what (indirect interrogative; dezir vos he que faze 'I shall tell you what he does'; = qué)
avedes: aver — you have (2nd pl. present, -edes; perfect auxiliary with a participle, me avedes mandado 'you have granted me'; = habéis)
vos: vos — you (object pronoun, polite/plural) · also subject 'you' (vos, que por mí dexades 'you who leave for my sake'); dative 'to you' (dar vos quiero vuestra part) · also reflexive/ethic 'you (yourselves)' (id vos en algara 'go off on a raid'); dative with an impersonal sense (si cueta vos fore 'if need befall you')
nada: nada — nothing; por nada 'for anything (in the world)'
vayamos: ir — let us go (present subjunctive 1st pl., exhortative; = vayamos)
posar: posar — to lodge, halt for the night (infinitive; = posar)
ca: ca — for, because (Latin quia) · ca — perhaps 'but, whereas' (el uno es en paradiso, ca el otro non entró allá; the sense is uncertain)
es: seer — it is (present 3rd sg.) · also ser as perfect auxiliary of intransitives (exido es 'has gone out') and passive auxiliary (la tienda es cogida) · also es — that (apocopated esse = ese, demonstrative; en es alcaz 'in that pursuit', por es logar 'through that place')
dixo: dezir — he/she said (strong preterite; x = sh-sound; = dijo)
plazme: plazer + me — it pleases me (plaze + enclitic me; = me place)
desta: de + esta — of this (preposition de + demonstrative fem. sg.; desta batalla 'of this battle'; = de esta)
presentaja: presentaja — gift, present (dar en presentaja 'to give as a gift'; Pidal: 'presente, regalo') · also an offer, a price proposed (d'aquesta presentaja 'with this offer'; Pidal: 'oferta o proposición de precio'); no modern form, closest presente, oferta
antes: antes — before; antes de 'before' · also antes que — 'before' (conjunction; antes quel prendan 'before they take him') · also antes — 'rather' (antes perderé el cuerpo 'rather shall I lose my body')
deste: de + este — of this, from this (contraction; deste pan 'of this bread', partitive 'some of'; = de este)
terçer: terçero — third (apocopated before a noun; al terçer día 'on the third day'; = tercer)
a: a — to, at · also aver — he/she has (3rd sg. present, h-less spelling of ha, as in el rey me a ayrado = el rey me ha airado) · personal a before a direct object (salvest a Jonás; a ti adoro); a + inf. 'to, about to' (tornólas a catar); a tan grand sabor 'with so great pleasure'; a ojo 'in plain sight' · also a — 'into' (sacar a çelada 'to lure into ambush'); 'at, in' (a la çaga 'at the rear'); 'against' (dar salto a la çaga); dative 'to' (a mí dedes); haber a + inf. 'have to' (lo han a far); a + noun of direction (adeliñava a la puerta 'made for the gate') · impersonal 'there is' (aver; es dia a de plazo 'there is (only) a day of the term', the most likely reading of a hard line); ha as auxiliary set after the participle (soñado a 'he has dreamt') · also 'on, at (a time)' (a tercer dia 'on the third day') · also a — 'has' before the participle, agreeing with the object (la lança a quebrada 'he has broken the lance'; a menester 'has need of'); a + dative of the person affected (a Minaya matáronle el cavallo 'they killed Minaya's horse') · a — 'as, for' (tóvoslo a grand fonta 'he took it as a great affront')
en: en — in, into, on · en — of it, thence (= ende; por en avemos qué fablar 'of which we have to speak') · also en — 'as' (en paria 'as tribute'); en essora 'at that moment' · also en — 'among' (en todos los sos 'among all his men') · also en + infinitive 'in (doing)' (en levarlo adelant 'in carrying it forward'); en çinco días 'in five days'
medina: Medina — Medinaceli, the frontier town on the Jalón where Alfonso's land ends (= Medinaceli)
alegres: alegre — glad, happy (pl.; todos son alegres 'all are glad'; = alegres)
del: de + el — of the (contraction) · also del standing for de + la before a feminine noun beginning with a vowel (del albergada = de la albergada)
portero: portero — the king's officer (Pidal: the palace official who replaced the old sayón, at first bringing persons into the king's presence, then carrying the king's letters and orders and carrying out his commands; not a door-keeper here; levedes un portero 'take a royal officer with you'; = portero real)
quitar: quitar — to leave, quit (infinitive; el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'; = quitar, closest abandonar) · also 'to set free' (quiero las i quitar 'I mean to free them there'; Pidal: 'libertar')
mandava: mandar — he ordered, was ordering (imperfect 3rd sg.; a sos creenderos guardar lo mandava 'he told his trusted men to guard him'; = mandaba)
ondrado: ondrar — honored, esteemed (past part. as adjective, masc. sg.; rey ondrado 'honored king'; = honrado)
mio: mio — my (unstressed possessive; mio Çid 'my lord Cid')
valençia: Valençia — Valencia, the Moorish kingdom and city whose king Tamín is addressed (= Valencia)
do: do — where, as (relative adverb, Latin de ubi; = donde) · also do — wherever, whenever (generalizing, with subjunctive: do yo vos enbiás 'wherever I might send you'; the exact sense is uncertain) · also dar — I give (present 1st sg.; d'aquí vos do mi graçia 'from here I give you my favor'; = doy)
conducho: conducho — provisions, victuals (Latin conductus; covers everything an army eats)
commo: commo — as, like (spelling variant of como) · how, that, in the way that (commo sirva a doña Ximena 'how he is to serve doña Ximena'); like (commo la uña de la carne) · also commo si + imperfect subjunctive — 'as if' (commo si escapasse 'as if he were fleeing') · commo que 'as one who' (commo que ira a de rey … es echado 'as one who has the king's anger and is cast out') · also commo — 'as soon as, when' (commo gelo a dicho 'as soon as he told it him'); 'since, as' (commo fío por Dios 'as I trust in God')
pagó: pagar — he paid, rewarded (preterite 3rd sg.; qué bien pagó a todos sus vassallos 'how well he paid all his vassals'; = pagó)
todo: todo — all, every (de todo conducho, 'with every kind of provision')
quito: quitar — I leave, give up (present 1st sg.) · also quitar — 'I release, pardon, lift the ban on' (a vos quito, Minaya 'I pardon you, Minaya'; = perdono)
va: ir — he/she goes (present 3rd sg.; = va); ir + gerund, 'to be (gradually) doing' · ir + infinitive 'goes to' (la manol va besar 'goes to kiss his hand', el Duero va passar 'goes to cross the Duero') · also va — 'there is, goes on' impersonal (¡Qué priessa va en los moros! 'what a stir there is among the Moors!')
mañana: mañana — morning (a la mañana 'in the morning'; otro dia mañana 'next morning'; = mañana) · also mañana — early, soon (adverb/predicate; mucho es mañana 'it is too soon (to take back a man in disgrace after only three weeks)'; = pronto, temprano)
salieron: salir — they went out (preterite 3rd pl.; = salieron)
salón: Salón — the river Jalón (the old form of the name; = Jalón)
arbuxuelo: Arbuxuelo — Arbujuelo, a small valley and stream feeding the Jalón, running down to Medinaceli (Pidal; val de Arbuxuelo, the ue restored by Pidal; = Arbujuelo)
arriba: arriba — up, upward (adverb; = arriba) · also postposed 'up, upstream' (Fenares arriba 'up the Henares'; desí arriba 'from there upward')
aguijavan: aguijar — they were spurring on, hastening (imperfect 3rd pl.; = aguijaban)
campo: campo — field, open ground, field of battle (= campo; en el campo 'in the open field'; the element in Campeador) · campo de Taranz 'the plain of Taranz'
taranz: Taranz — campo de Taranz, part of the plateau dividing the waters of the Tajuña and the Jalón, on the border of the provinces of Guadalajara and Soria (Pidal)
molina: Molina — Molina (de Aragón), town in the province of Guadalajara (= Molina)
don: don — don, lord (honorific title) · also don — gift (noun; en don 'as a gift') · also don — from where, whence (= donde, de onde; Castejón don abremos grand enpara 'Castejón, from which we shall have great protection') · 'whereof, with which' (Pidal 'de lo cual'; don yo sea pagado 'whereof I may be satisfied') · also don — when, where (= donde, of time; Don llegan los otros 'when the others come up')
jerome: Jerome — Jerónimo, the Cid's bishop of Valencia (Pidal restores Jero[me], 'don Jerome'; = Jerónimo)
las: el/la — the (fem. pl.); them (fem. object pronoun)
noches: noche — night (fem. pl.; las noches e los días 'nights and days'; = noches)
los: el — the (masc. pl.); them (object pronoun) · also los que 'those who' (demonstrative use before a relative); los — him, them as object of consejar (commo los consejava 'as he advised them') · also los de 'those of' (con los de Castejón 'with the men of Castejón')
diestro: diestro — right (hand, side), noun use (de diestro 'on the right'; = diestro, closest derecha) · also diestro — adjective 'right' (so diestro braço 'his right arm'); mio diestro braço 'my right arm', figuratively my chief support
ante: ante — before; ante que 'before (that)' · also ante — because of, at (of the cause, like Latin prae; ante roído de atamores 'at the din of the drums')
sues: su — his, her (fem. pl. possessive, old sue/sues; = sus)
armas: arma — weapon, arms (pl.; armas de lidiar 'weapons for fighting'; en armas 'in arms, armed'; = armas) · also armas — men-at-arms, armed men (treynta mill de armas 'thirty thousand armed men')
entre: entre — between, among; entre X e Y 'X and Y together'
él: él — he (stressed subject pronoun) · also él — 'him, it' after a preposition, of a thing (a él vino; en él fincaredes 'in it', i.e. in Castejón)
compaña: conpaña — company, retinue (= compañía; spelling variant with m of conpaña)
son: seer — they are (3rd pl.) · also son — perfect auxiliary of intransitives and passive auxiliary (todos son exidos 'have all gone out'; nombrados son; son derramadas 'are scattered')
buena: bueno — good (fem.); en buen(a) '(born/girded) in a good hour' — the poem's honorific formula
casa: casa — house; also settlement, town (Burgos la casa 'the town of Burgos')
moro: moro — Moor, Muslim (noun; el moro Avengalvón 'the Moor Avengalvón'; = moro)
bien: bien — well · bien — good, benefit (noun; algún bien vos pueda far 'some good I may do you') · bien — very, quite, intensifying an adverb (bien çerca del agua 'very near the water')
quanto: quanto — as much as, whatever (= cuanto) · quanto ella mejor sabe 'as best she can' (quanto + comparative 'as much as') · also 'how much' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'as far/fast as' (quanto pueden andar) · tanto quanto 'as long as'; por quanto … ha 'for all that there is' (por quanto en el mundo ha)
ovieron: aver — they had, they got (strong preterite of aver; = hubieron) · also ovieron a + inf. — 'they had to, were obliged to' (ovieron a enbiar 'they had to send'; = tuvieron que enviar)
aun: aun — even, besides · also aun — yet, still (aun vea el dia 'may I yet see the day') · also 'even though' (= aunque; aun de lo que diessen oviessen grand ganançia, Pidal's reading)
gelas: ge + las — them for/to him (ge, ancestor of modern se, + las; = se las)
otro: otro — other, another (masc.; el otro 'the other'; = otro) · also otro día 'the next day'; lo otro 'the rest'
fata: fata — until, as far as (variant of fasta; = hasta)
so: so/su — his, her, its (unstressed possessive sg.; so çervicio = su servicio); also seer — I am (1st sg. present; = soy; so ayrado, 'I am in [the king's] ira') · lo so — 'what is his, his own' (neuter article + possessive; lo so puede menguar 'what is his may dwindle') · also so — their (so consejo 'their counsel', so vino 'their wine'; = su)
dellos: de + ellos — of them, from them (contraction)
nuevas: nueva — news, tidings (fem. pl.; sus nuevas legavan 'his news was arriving'; = noticias, nuevas) · also nuevas — renown, fame (las nuevas de mio Çid sonando van; Pidal 'renombre, fama') · also nuevas — affairs, doings (las nuevas del cavallero 'the knight's affairs'; Pidal 'los asuntos, los negocios') · also nuevas — exploits, deeds (las nuevas que faze el Campeador; Pidal 'las hazañas que hace')
aprés: aprés — near, close by (preposition, with de; aprés de la uerta 'close by the orchard-land'; no modern form, = cerca de, junto a)
çinxo: çeñir — he girded (strong preterite 3rd sg.; Latin cinxit)
fo: seer (and ir, which shares this preterite) — he/it was; went (preterite 3rd sg.; = fue, restored by Pidal as f[o]; of this part's three occurrences, fo entrado and fo acusado are periphrastic/passive ser + past part. constructions, while fo algo is a plain copula with a pronoun predicate, 'was something') · also commo fo tu voluntad, ca fo tu voluntad 'as/for it was your will' (ser + noun subject, 'it was'; Pidal restores f[o]) · also se fo acomendar 'went to commend himself' (ir); fo de noch 'it was night' (ser de + noun, 'night had come'); fo desenparada (passive, 'was abandoned') · also fo — went (ir; mañanas fo Minaya 'in the morning Minaya went'); fo de moros 'it came from the Moors' (ser de + noun of origin; Pidal restores f[o]) · also fo — it was, ser + adjective predicate (Buena fo la de Valençia 'good was the (capture) of Valencia'; Pidal restores f[o])
más: más — more; e más 'and moreover' · non más 'no more, nothing more'; por que más valdrá 'whereby he will be worth more'
tanto: tanto — so much, so great · tanto quanto + subjunctive 'as long as' (tanto quanto yo biva 'as long as I live')
mandado: mandado — message, news, word (noun; from mandar 'to send, order') · also mandado — order, command (mandado de so señor 'the lord's command'); fazer mandado 'to send word' · also past part. 'granted, assigned' (el quinto que me avedes mandado 'the fifth you have granted me')
mandó: mandar — he ordered (preterite 3rd sg.; = mandó) · also mandar — 'he held, governed' a place (Çorita mandó 'he held Çorita'; el que mandó a Mont Mayor 'he who governed Mont Mayor')
exir: exir — to go out, leave (infinitive; = salir)
dalgo: de + algo — of something; fija dalgo 'daughter of something', well-born (= hidalga)
trahe: traer — brings (present 3rd sg., h marking the old hiatus; fuerças que trahe 'the forces he brings'; = trae)
recabdo: recabdo — care, precaution, strict order (= recaudo) · also recabdo — business secured, a sure outcome (con todo buen recabdo 'with everything well in hand') · recabdo — account, reckoning (oro e plata que non saben recabdo 'gold and silver past all reckoning') · also con recabdo — within bounds, under control (non es con recabdo el dolor de Valençia 'the grief of Valencia is past all bounds') · also todo el recabdo está 'every precaution is taken' (Pidal: 'hay toda clase de precauciones'; en Medina todo el recabdo está)
afevos: afevos — behold, here is/are (presentative, a + fe + vos; = he aquí, ahí tenéis)
aquestos: aqueste — these (masc. pl., 'aqueste' = este with prefixed aque-; aquestos dos reyes 'these two kings'; = estos)
conpañas: conpaña — company, retinue, band of followers (pl.; = compañas)
ha: aver — he has (3rd sg. present; = ha) · ha — to (a with h-, aver a + inf. 'will, must': lo an todos ha far 'all are to do it'); aver — has, possesses (las fijas que ha 'the daughters she has') · also ha — future ending after infinitive + clitics, the split future (tornar nos la ha 'he will give it back to us'; = nos la tornará) · also ha — there is, there are (impersonal; dos señas ha cabdales 'there are two chief banners'; = hay) · also ha — perfect auxiliary 'has' before the participle (ha vendido 'has sold'; fechos los ha ricos 'has made them rich') · also 'has, gets' (de señor non ha graçia 'he has no favor from a lord') · also ha de + inf. 'is to' (que los ha de aguardar 'who is to attend them'; aver de + infinitive, = ha de)
alcáçer: alcáçer — citadel, fortress (Arabic al-qaṣr; en somo del alcáçer 'on top of the citadel'; = alcázar)
exidas: exida — way out, exit, sally (fem. pl., from exir; las exidas e las entradas 'the ways out and the ways in', i.e. the passes; = salidas)
entradas: entrada — way in, entrance, approach (fem. pl.; las exidas e las entradas; = entradas)
avié: aver — he had (imperfect of aver = haber, here a full verb 'to have, hold') · also impersonal 'there was' (mucho avié grant plaça 'there was a very great space'; = había) · also avié — auxiliary 'had' + participle, pluperfect (avié dado 'he had given'; = había dado)
quel: que + le — who ... him (que + enclitic/elided le) · that ... to him (quel creçe conpaña 'that company grows for him')
d: de — of, with (elided form of de before a vowel, d'arena = de arena) · de — from (unos d'otros 'one from another')
aquel: aquel — that one, whoever · also aquel — that (demonstrative adjective; aquel día de cras 'tomorrow'; aquella mayor az 'that biggest line')
sevilla: Sevilla — Seville; from 1091 held by the Almoravids, so rey de Sevilla is the Almoravid general who governed it (Pidal's note to v. 1222; = Sevilla)
arrancada: arrancada — rout, headlong flight; also the pursuit and rout of the enemy (de arrancada 'in rout'; el arrancada, el before a vowel-initial fem. noun; = arrancada) · also 'victory' (Pidal's gloss at v. 1233: esta arrancada 'this victory')
ora: hora — hour (= hora); en buen ora, part of the poem's honorific birth-formula, 'born in a good hour' · al ora 'at that very hour, then' (en ti crovo al ora)
serié: seer — it would be (conditional 3rd sg.; = sería)
o: o — or; also ó — where (interrogative, Latin ubi; ¿O sodes…? 'Where are you…?') · also o — where (relative adverb; o dizen Castejón 'which they call Castejón'; o el Campeador estava 'where the Campeador was'; = donde) · correlative 'either … or' (o me dexaredes … o … levaredes 'either you will leave me … or you will take away')
salvo: salvo — safety, safe-keeping (noun; en vuestro salvo 'in your safe keeping') · also adjective, safe, saved (por end es salvo de mal 'for that reason he is saved from evil')
delante: delante — in front, ahead, before (adverb, fuller form of delant; váyante delante 'may they go before you'; = delante)
su: su — his, her, its · also su — their (aquella su almofalla 'that host of theirs')
querié: querer — it was about to (imperfect 3rd sg., -ié ending; la noch querié entrar 'night was about to fall'; = quería) · also querer — he wished (imperfect 3rd sg.; commo querié trasnochar 'how he wished to travel by night'; = quería)
tener: tener — to hold, keep (infinitive, first element of the split future tener la edes 'you will hold it'; = tener)
y: y — and (rarer spelling of e) · also y — there (adverb, = i, Latin ibi; entraré y 'I shall enter there')
adeliñava: adeliñar — he was making straight for (imperfect 3rd sg.; = adeliñaba; no modern equivalent, closest dirigirse a)
quantos: quanto — as many as (masc. pl.; todos quantos 'all who'; = cuantos)
vestidas: vestir — put on, clad in (past part. fem. pl.; = vestidas)
bueno: bueno — good, fine, great (qué bueno es el gozo 'how great is the joy'; = bueno)
nasco: nacer — he was born (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = nació)
detardava: detardar — was delaying (imperfect 3rd sg.; = tardaba, se retrasaba)
luenga: luengo — long (fem. sg., Latin longus; la luenga barba 'the long beard'; modern luengo survives only archaically, = larga)
cuberturas: cubertura — horse-covering, caparison (pl.; cuberturas de çendales 'caparisons of silk'; = cobertura, closest gualdrapa)
le: le — to him, him (dative pronoun) · also le — him, as direct object (leísmo; si ellos le prenden 'if they take him'); dative (non se le dava 'did not surrender to him') · also le — dative of separation, 'from him' (que nos le parte de so braço 'who does not leave his side'); dative 'for him' (ques le non spidiés 'who does not take leave of him')
sobrél: sobre + él — over him, beside him (preposition + pronoun, the e of sobre dropped; sobrél sedie 'he sat beside him', Pidal 'junto a él estaba')
por: por — through, along, by, for · purpose, 'in order to' (por el reyno quitar 'to quit the kingdom'); por + inf. 'yet to be done' (tres an por troçir 'three remain to pass'); 'for, on behalf of' (por mio Çid) · also por — 'out of, because of' (por miedo 'through fear'); 'for (that reason)' (por tal lo faze 'he does it for that reason'); 'by way of' (por Guadalfajara); por + noun 'for the sake of' ; por coraçón 'willingly' · also 'for (a price)' (por quanto serié conprada 'for how much it would be bought'); 'by means of' (por carta 'by writ'); 'through, thanks to' (por mí ganaredes 'through me you will gain') · also por — 'on, during (a time)' (por aquesta mañana 'this morning'); 'by way of, through' (por medio de la llaña 'through the middle of the plain') · also por — 'in' after fiar (yo fío por Dios 'I trust in God') · also por — 'to fetch, for' after enbiar/ir (enbiaré por ellas, irán por ellas 'I shall send for them', 'they will go for them'); por cuenta 'by count, in a count' · also por — as (por heredad 'as a possession')
nombre: nombre — name; por nombre 'by name, called' (= nombre)
fizo: fazer — he made, did, caused (strong preterite 3rd sg.; fizo posar 'he made (them) halt'; = hizo)
corrida: corrida — raid, foray (noun from correr; fizo una corrida 'he made a raid'; = corrida, closest correría)
estraña: estraño — extraordinary, remarkable, great (fem.; priessa much estraña 'a most extraordinary rush'; = extraña) · also estraño — foreign, strange (tierra estraña 'a foreign land'; = extraña)
ovo: aver — he had (strong preterite 3rd sg.; = hubo; here perfect auxiliary, ovo bastidos = 'he had furnished') · ovo de + inf., little more than a plain past (las manos se ovo de untar 'his hands were smeared'); dont a ojo los ovo 'as soon as he had them in sight'
cabo: cabo — beside, next to (preposition; cf. modern cabe) · also cabo — end (noun; fasta cabo del año, 'until the end of the year') · also de cabo — 'again, anew' (que los cometamos de cabo 'that we attack them again'; = de nuevo) · also a cabo de — at the end of, after (a cabo de tres sedmanas 'after three weeks')
adeliñó: adeliñar — he made straight for, headed to (preterite)
amas: amos — both (fem. pl., Latin ambas; las manos amas 'both hands'; = ambas)
doña: doña — lady (title; Latin domina, fem. of don)
piedes: pie — feet (old plural, Latin pedes; los piedes e las manos 'the feet and the hands'; = pies) · also de piedes de cavallo 'at full gallop' (Pidal 'a uña de caballo')
echava: echar — he was lying down, throwing himself (imperfect 3rd sg., -ava; echarse 'to lie down'; i se echava 'he lay down there'; = echaba)
campeador: Campeador — the Battler, the Champion (the Cid's epithet, from campo 'field of battle')
cinxiestes: çeñir — you girded (strong preterite 2nd pl., respectful to one person; = ceñisteis)
muchas: mucho — many (fem. pl.; muchas son las arrobdas 'many are the watches'; = muchas)
aquí: aquí — here; d'aquí 'from here' · also 'then, at this point' (aquí dixo el comde 'then the count said')
convusco: con + vusco — with you (fused form; cf. con vusco, v. 75)
sos: so — his, her, their (= modern sus) · also los sos 'his own men' (possessive with article as noun; en todos los sos 'among all his men')
mesnadas: mesnada — household troop, band of followers (pl.; = mesnadas)
ondrada: ondrar — honored, splendid (past part. fem. used as adj.; = honrada)
coraçón: coraçón — heart (= corazón) · also por coraçón 'willingly, heartily, with a will' (lo an por coraçón)
mi: mi — my (unstressed possessive) · also mi — me (stressed pronoun after a preposition; por mi 'on my behalf'; = mí)
comigo: comigo — with me (con + migo, Latin mecum; = conmigo)
heredad: heredad — inherited holding, estate, landed property (por heredad 'as a possession'; = heredad)
he: aver — I have (1st sg. present; perfect auxiliary, = he, and the auxiliary of the split future, e.g. doblar vos he)
ganada: ganar — taken, won (past part. fem. sg., agreeing with the object la; ganada se la a 'he has taken it for himself'; = ganada)
manos: mano — hand (pl.); dar las manos = the handclasp that makes an agreement binding · a las manos 'for the hands' (pidió agua a las manos 'asked for water to wash his hands'); bolver las manos 'to ply the hands', busy eating
ellas: ella — they, them (fem. pl., stressed; con ellas 'with them'; = ellas)
entravan: entrar — they were entering (imperfect 3rd pl.; = entraban)
